introduction: Utah’s earned income tax credit is claimed with the state income-tax return. It is a nonrefundable tax reduction, not a separate benefit application.
description: Utah’s earned income tax credit is claimed with the state income-tax return. It is a nonrefundable tax reduction, not a separate benefit application.

sections.who: The state instructions require a federal EITC claimed in the same year and Utah wages reported on a W-2.
sections.get: A qualifying credit reduces state tax liability under the TC-40A worksheet.
sections.docs:
• Federal return showing EITC.
  • W-2 showing Utah wages.
  • State return and TC-40A worksheet.
sections.apply:
1. Check the filing-year instructions

    Use TC-40A instructions.

  2. Complete the worksheet

    Use the federal credit and Utah wage entries.

  3. Claim code AM

    Enter the allowed credit in TC-40A Part 3 with the state return.
sections.after: Save the return and worksheet. Follow Tax Commission notices if any entry needs clarification.
sections.sources: Checked October 1, 2026 using Utah EITC worksheet and code AM. USA Assistance background guide. Program staff determine eligibility and available assistance.

faqs: The state lists it as nonrefundable.
Can an unused amount carry forward?
The instructions say excess credit cannot be carried forward or back.
Is a federal credit alone sufficient?
Utah also requires qualifying Utah W-2 income.

provenance.scope: Published eligibility, service purpose and application pathway; no unverified financial limits or deadlines included.
